fields.mechanism: Antifouling surface coating that chemically resists adhesion of biological or material deposits, as evidenced by heparin coating’s anticoagulant effect.
fields.intervention: Incorporate a marine‑grade polymer anti‑biofouling coating (e.g., copper‑based or silicone‑based fouling‑release polymer) onto catheter surfaces to create a non‑thrombogenic interface.
fields.expected_effect: Similar reduction in thrombus adherence, extending catheter patency without reliance on heparin.
fields.falsification_test: In‑vitro flow loop comparing standard catheters, heparin‑coated catheters, and catheters with marine anti‑fouling coating for clot formation over 14 days.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin coating on catheter surface reduces thrombus formation, extending failure‑free survival.
fields.intervention: Replace the active heparin coating with a passive, non‑fouling hydrophilic polymer (e.g., PEG or zwitterionic) layer on the catheter lumen to physically deter protein and platelet adhesion, thereby maintaining patency without releasing anticoagulant.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained flow patency for weeks comparable to heparin‑coated catheters, with reduced occlusion rates under standard flushing protocols.
fields.falsification_test: Perform a randomized bench‑flow experiment measuring time to occlusion under simulated blood flow and flushing, comparing heparin‑coated catheters, PEG‑coated catheters, and uncoated controls.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin coating on the catheter surface reduces thrombus formation within the lumen.
fields.intervention: Apply a continuous heparin‑bonded polymer coating to the inner lumen (and optionally outer surface) of the tunneled hemodialysis catheter during manufacturing.
fields.expected_effect: Maintains flow patency for weeks under standard flushing protocols, markedly decreasing catheter occlusion events.
fields.falsification_test: In a side‑by‑side bench study, expose heparin‑coated and uncoated catheters to simulated blood flow with periodic saline flushes; record time to pressure rise indicating occlusion over a 30‑day period.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin coating on the catheter surface prevents thrombus formation, maintaining lumen patency and fluid flow.
fields.intervention: Apply a durable heparin‑bonded polymer coating to both inner and outer surfaces of the tunneled catheter and add a helical micro‑groove pattern inside the lumen to generate secondary flow, thereby coupling chemical anticoagulation with fluidic shear enhancement.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained flow patency for weeks under standard flushing protocols, markedly reducing catheter occlusion and exchange rates.
fields.falsification_test: In a controlled blood‑loop bench test, compare time‑to‑occlusion of heparin‑coated, micro‑grooved catheters versus standard heparin‑coated catheters using identical flushing schedules; a statistically similar or shorter occlusion time would falsify the proposed benefit.
